messages:
hao: Quick thread to capture the cutover checklist from today's architecture sync. Focus: fastpath/control-plane split, RBAC migration, and renderer integration.

naya: Short recap: fastpath does tenant+route admit checks and returns lightweight payloads + optional pending token. Control-plane validates row-level entitlements and issues signed allowance blobs. Renderer merges final rows when allowance arrives.

leo: Two immediate concerns: (1) token format + verification, (2) per-tenant routing and emergency rollback.

priya: Token plan: use compact HMAC token for V1; fields: v|tid|route|exp|nonce|hmac. Keep TTL short (default 7s). Add nonce replay cache with size 2k per fastpath node. Ops wants KMS for signing.

hao: Addendum: every token must include key-id header so control-plane can select verification key during rotation. Documented in RFC addendum.

naya: Routing: store routing table in ConfigService and stream via SDS (simple delta). Routing entry example: {tenant, enabled_features, route_mode} where route_mode = legacy|fastpath|partial. We need fast toggles to force legacy per-tenant.

leo: Rollback hooks: (a) config gate in ConfigService, (b) legacy env toggle at runtime (FASTPATH_ENABLED=false), (c) emergency revert job that flips all tenants to legacy. Make sure revert is low-latency and idempotent.

priya: Migration strategy for RBAC buckets: dry-run audit -> sidecar tag writer for pilot tenants -> staggered backfill -> final cut. Backfill QPS target: 50 QPS to migration table initially, can ramp. Instrument `migration_backfill_qps`.

hao: Telemetry & SLOs: define `fastpath_latency_p50/p95/p99`, `controlplane_latency_p50/p95/p99`, `token_issuance_rate`, `token_replay_rate`, `rbac_migration_errors`, `renderer_merge_latency`. Set alert if controlplane_p95 > 400ms for 3m.

naya: UI contract: renderer should handle three scenarios: (A) immediate full payload (no token), (B) partial payload + pending token -> render skeleton + fill, (C) stale snapshot + pending token -> update when merged. Add tenant-level feature flag `ui_partial_updates` to opt in.

leo: Performance knobs: batching window default 10ms (config OP_BATCH_WINDOW_MS), per-node decision cache TTL 3s, cache size 4096. We'll test combinations in perf harness.

priya: Security: mTLS for control-plane <-> fastpath traffic, KMS for signing keys, key rotation quarterly. Add token replay mitigation and short-expiry. Ops: cert rotation plan required.

hao: Canary plan: start with internal infra tenant -> 5 small customers -> 20 mids -> enterprise blocked until logs/metrics stable. Each stage runs 1h smoke + 4h observation. Fallback step must be tested during canary.

naya: Observability runbook: traces must propagate through trace-id, include token id as trace tag, and capture decision cache hits. Dashboards: fastpath/controlplane comparisons and per-tenant fallback counts.

leo: Dev work items (owners & ETA): routing schema (naya, Thurs), token format + lib (priya, Fri), migration script dry-run (hao, Mon), perf harness (leo, Fri), runbooks + alerts (ops-team, Tues).

priya: Small ops note: when we run backfill we should rate-limit by tenant and use adaptive concurrency to avoid thundering herd. Use shard-based tokens for the job.

ops-bot: deploy initiated: `console-operator-fastpath:v1` -> canary-03 (sha: f2b7e9d) :rocket:

hao: If no objections I'll open the PR linking this thread and the RFC. Also will attach the canary checklist.

naya: Go ahead. One more: ensure the renderer ignores unknown headers to preserve backward compatibility.

leo: Thanks all — I captured notes in the RFC repo. We'll iterate on perf knobs after harness results.

ops-bot: canary completed: `console-operator-fastpath:v1` (cluster: canary-03) :white_check_mark:
